draft.title: Environmental awareness
card: From the 1960s, many people grew worried about pollution and damage to nature. Factories, chemicals and rubbish were harming air, water and wildlife.
Books and news reports helped spread the concern. Rachel Carson's book Silent Spring (1962) warned about the harm done by pesticides.
Concern led to environmental movements, which are groups of people working together to protect nature. Examples include protests to save forests and rivers.

Governments also passed laws to limit pollution and protect natural areas. In Australia, campaigns in the 1970s and 1980s, such as the one to save the Franklin River in Tasmania, put pressure on governments.
draft.remember: Worry about pollution led to movements and laws.

a.q: What did growing worry about pollution after the 1960s lead to?
opts: An end to all factory production
The creation of the United Nations
A fall in the use of television
a.why: People joined groups to protect nature, and governments passed laws to limit pollution. Factories did not stop all production, and the United Nations began in 1945, before this concern grew.

b.q: In the 1980s, residents of a town in Victoria gather to stop a factory dumping waste into their river. This is an example of what?
b.why: Residents working together to protect nature form an environmental movement. A law would be passed by a government, so it is the tempting wrong choice here.
b.clue: Who is acting: citizens or a government?

problems.detail: The question says worry 'after the 1960s', but the card says concern grew 'from the 1960s'. 'After the 1960s' suggests the 1970s onwards. It should say 'from the 1960s' to match the card.
